Drafting aid only. I work only from the documents in this project, cite every fact, and do not rate risk or recommend credit decisions. Verify citations before use.

## Section 3: Financial Analysis


Northwind Foodservice Distribution, LLC. $ in thousands unless stated. Fiscal year ends December 31. FY2023-FY2025 were audited by Kessling Marr LLP with unqualified opinions. [D1, header]

### 3.1 Revenue and Earnings

Revenue was 94,200 in FY2023, 99,800 in FY2024 and 104,600 in FY2025. [D1, Table 1: Revenue, FY2023-FY2025] Reported revenue growth was 6.6% in FY2023, 5.9% in FY2024 and 4.8% in FY2025. [D1, Table 1: Revenue growth, FY2023-FY2025] FY2022 revenue was 88,400 (audited). [D1, §1 Note to Table 1]

EBITDA was 4,200 in FY2023, 4,300 in FY2024 and 4,100 in FY2025. [D1, Table 1: EBITDA, FY2023-FY2025] EBITDA margin was 4.5% in FY2023, 4.3% in FY2024 and 3.9% in FY2025. [D1, Table 1: EBITDA margin, FY2023-FY2025] Net income was 2,290 in FY2023, 2,180 in FY2024 and 1,870 in FY2025. [D1, Table 1: Net income, FY2023-FY2025]

Trailing-four-quarter EBITDA was 4,240 at Q1 2025, 4,120 at Q2 2025, 3,980 at Q3 2025, 4,100 at Q4 2025, 4,020 at Q1 2026 and 3,950 at Q2 2026. [D1, Table 3: EBITDA (TTM), Q1 2025-Q2 2026] Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 figures are from internally prepared quarterly statements. [D1, §3 Note to Table 3]

Management commentary, per the analyst's summary of the borrower's FY2025 letter: "Revenue grew 4.8% in FY2025 on new independent restaurant accounts. Fuel and warehouse labor costs rose faster than case prices." [D1, §6] Management also expects a route optimization project, completed in May 2026, to reduce delivery cost per case. [D1, §6]

Customer A, a regional restaurant group, accounted for 21% of FY2024 revenue and 23% of FY2025 revenue. [D1, §5] The top five customers accounted for 47% of FY2025 revenue. [D1, §5]

CONFLICT: The management commentary states "EBITDA was about $4.5 million for the year." [D1, §6] The spread reports FY2025 EBITDA of 4,100. [D1, Table 1: EBITDA, FY2025] Neither value is chosen.

### 3.2 Leverage and Debt Service

Total funded debt was 10,710 in FY2023, 12,040 in FY2024 and 13,120 in FY2025. [D1, Table 2: Total funded debt, FY2023-FY2025] At FY2025 it comprised the Meridian term loan at 1,600, the Meridian revolver at 8,100 and fleet capital leases (Ridgeway Truck Finance) at 3,420. [D1, §4: FY2025]

Total leverage was 2.55x in FY2023, 2.80x in FY2024 and 3.20x in FY2025. [D1, Table 2: Total leverage, FY2023-FY2025] DSCR was 1.45x in FY2023, 1.36x in FY2024 and 1.27x in FY2025. [D1, Table 2: DSCR, FY2023-FY2025]

Spread DSCR components:

- Unfunded capex was 600 in FY2023, 650 in FY2024 and 700 in FY2025. [D1, Table 1: Unfunded capex, FY2023-FY2025]
- Cash taxes were 700 in FY2023, 680 in FY2024 and 600 in FY2025. [D1, Table 1: Cash taxes, FY2023-FY2025]
- Debt service (P+I) was 2,000 in FY2023, 2,180 in FY2024 and 2,200 in FY2025. [D1, Table 1: Debt service (P+I), FY2023-FY2025]

Quarterly covenant-test figures, trailing four quarters, as reported in the borrower's compliance certificates [D1, §3 Note to Table 3]:

| Row | Q1 2025 | Q2 2025 | Q3 2025 | Q4 2025 | Q1 2026 | Q2 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total funded debt | 12,700 | 13,250 | 13,570 | 13,120 | 13,000 | 13,350 |
| Total leverage | 3.00x | 3.22x | 3.41x | 3.20x | 3.23x | 3.38x |
| DSCR | 1.33x | 1.28x | 1.22x | 1.27x | 1.25x | 1.24x |

[D1, Table 3: Total funded debt, Total leverage, DSCR, Q1 2025-Q2 2026]

The credit agreement sets a maximum Total Leverage Ratio of 3.75 to 1.00 and a minimum Debt Service Coverage Ratio of 1.20 to 1.00, each as of the last day of any fiscal quarter. [D2, §7.1; D2, §7.2] Each certificate from Q1 2025 to Q2 2026 reported compliance with both financial covenants. [D1, §7]

### 3.3 Liquidity

Cash was 1,400 in FY2023, 1,100 in FY2024 and 900 in FY2025. [D1, Table 2: Cash, FY2023-FY2025] Revolver availability was 3,100 in FY2023 and 2,400 in FY2024. [D1, Table 2: Revolver availability, FY2023-FY2024] Liquidity (cash + availability) was 4,500 in FY2023 and 3,500 in FY2024. [D1, Table 2: Liquidity, FY2023-FY2024]

Not in provided documents: FY2025 revolver availability and FY2025 liquidity. The December 31, 2025 Borrowing Base Certificate was not included in the spread export. [D1, §2 Footnote *] Credit Administration will attach it to the annual review package. [D1, §2 Footnote *]

Not in provided documents: revolver availability or Excess Availability at Q1 2026, Q2 2026 or any later date. Borrowing Base Certificates (due monthly) would normally contain it. [D2, §7.4(d)]

The Meridian revolver balance was 4,900 in FY2023, 6,600 in FY2024 and 8,100 in FY2025. [D1, §4: Meridian revolver, FY2023-FY2025] The Revolving Commitment is $10,000,000. [D2, §2.1(b)]

The credit agreement states: "The Borrower shall not permit Excess Availability to be less than $1,000,000 at any time." [D2, §7.3] The compliance certificates do not report Excess Availability under the minimum availability covenant. [D1, §7]

Average operating deposits at Meridian were $2.3 million over the trailing 12 months to August 2026. [D5, ¶2]

### 3.4 Pro Forma for Proposed Facility

No facility change is proposed [D1, §3 Note to Table 3] or was requested at the September 10, 2026 annual review call. [D5, ¶5] The existing facility totals $14.0M: a $4.0M term loan and a $10.0M revolver. [D1, §3 Note to Table 3]

Not in provided documents: pro forma total leverage, pro forma DSCR and any pro forma debt schedule. A proposed-facility sizing or pro forma model would normally contain them.

**Sources used:** D1 (header; §1 Table 1 and Note; §2 Table 2 and Footnote *; §3 Table 3 and Note; §4; §5; §6; §7); D2 (§2.1(b); §7.1; §7.2; §7.3; §7.4(d)); D5 (¶2; ¶5).

**Underwriter to complete:**
- **Section 3.5 Underwriter Commentary [U]:** this subsection is underwriter-authored and has not been drafted. Cited facts the underwriter may need:
  - The Q2 2025 compliance certificate arrived 25 days late and the reporting covenant was waived under W-25-0388. [D5, ¶3]
  - The CFO attributed the Q3 2025 DSCR change to diesel and warehouse wage costs and to a school district contract not renewed in July 2025. [D5, ¶4]
  - The CFO said no tax distributions above the members' estimated tax liability are planned in FY2026. [D5, ¶4]
  - Dale Ostrander plans to step back as CEO in mid-2027, and the family has discussed selling up to 30% of the membership interests to an ESOP, with no timeline and no engagement letter. [D5, ¶5]
- **CONFLICT:** FY2025 EBITDA is 4,100 in the spread [D1, Table 1] and "about $4.5 million" in management commentary [D1, §6]. Resolve with the borrower or Credit Analysis.
- **Gap:** FY2025 revolver availability and liquidity, and availability at Q1 2026 and Q2 2026. These need the Borrowing Base Certificates. Excess Availability against the $1,000,000 minimum in D2 §7.3 is not reported in any compliance certificate. [D1, §7]
- **Definition check:** the spread defines DSCR using "unfunded capex," "cash taxes" and "Debt service (P+I)." [D1, §2 definitions] D2 §1.1 defines it using Unfinanced Capital Expenditures, cash taxes paid including Permitted Tax Distributions, and scheduled principal and interest including interest on the Revolving Loans. Confirm the spread matches the D2 definitions. The spread EBITDA basis against the D2 EBITDA definition is also unverified.
- **Pro forma (3.4):** no pro forma figures are provided. The underwriter should determine whether D4 §4.2.1-§4.2.3 pro forma tests apply to this annual review with no facility change.
- **Policy item needing judgment:** D4 §4.2.4 concentration language applies to Section 7. Customer A's FY2025 share is stated in §3.1 above. [D1, §5; D4, §4.2.4]

### Items for legal and underwriter review

**Undefined or missing terms**
- "Capital Lease Obligations" appears in the Total Funded Debt definition and §7.5(b)(ii) but is not defined in the excerpt. [D2, §1.1; D2, §7.5(b)] The excerpt says undefined capitalized terms take their meanings from the full agreement. [D2, header]
- Schedule 1.1 (Eligible Inventory) is not included. [D2, §1.1] This affects the Borrowing Base and therefore Excess Availability under §7.3.
- Default, cure, grace-period and remedy provisions other than §7.6 are not in the excerpt. Not in provided documents: the Events of Default section and any cure rights the full D2 agreement would contain.

**Ambiguous wording (quoted, not interpreted)**
- §7.6: "cease to control," "primary responsibility for the operations," "reasonably satisfactory to the Lender" and "within a reasonable period." Refer to legal.
- §7.4(a): "an independent accounting firm acceptable to the Lender." The excerpt states no acceptance criteria. [D2, §7.4(a)]
- §7.3: "at any time" is a continuous test; the Borrowing Base Certificate is delivered monthly as of month-end. [D2, §7.3; D2, §7.4(d)] Refer to legal on how the two operate together.
- §7.4(b) and (c) require quarterly statements and Compliance Certificates for the first three fiscal quarters. The fourth quarter is covered by the annual delivery under §7.4(a). [D2, §7.4(a)-(c)] Refer to legal to confirm the intended Q4 mechanics.
- Borrowing Base reserves are set "in its reasonable credit judgment." [D2, §1.1]

**Spread definitions against D2 definitions (underwriter to verify)**
- D2 defines the DSCR numerator using "cash taxes paid (including Permitted Tax Distributions)" and Unfinanced Capital Expenditures. [D2, §1.1] The spread labels these "Cash taxes" and "Unfunded capex." [D1, §1 Table 1; D1, §2 definitions]
- D2 defines the DSCR denominator as scheduled principal and interest on Total Funded Debt, "including interest on the Revolving Loans." [D2, §1.1] The spread labels it "Debt service (P+I)." [D1, §2 definitions]

**Compliance reporting facts for the review**
- Per D1, compliance certificates do not report Excess Availability under the minimum availability covenant. [D1, §7]
- Not in provided documents: Borrowing Base Certificates and any Excess Availability figure. They are due monthly under D2 §7.4(d). [D2, §7.4(d)] The December 31, 2025 certificate was not in the spread export. [D1, §2 Footnote *]
- The Q2 2025 compliance certificate arrived 25 days late. Credit Administration waived the "reporting covenant" under waiver W-25-0388. [D5, ¶3] The notes do not identify the clause waived. Not in provided documents: the waiver document, which Credit Administration would hold.

**Facts relevant to the §7.6 review (no interpretation given)**
- Dale Ostrander (67) plans to step back as CEO in mid-2027; Megan Ostrander-Kolb is expected to take over day-to-day operations. [D5, ¶5]
- The family has discussed selling up to 30% of membership interests to an employee stock ownership plan, with no timeline and no engagement letter. [D5, ¶5]
- Ownership: Dale Ostrander 60%, Ruth Ostrander 20%, Megan Ostrander-Kolb 20%. [D5, ¶1]

**Not extracted as covenants**
- The Term Loan repayment schedule (quarterly installments of $200,000, balance due December 15, 2027) and the revolver termination date of December 15, 2027 are payment terms. [D2, §2.1(a)-(b)]
- The use-of-proceeds sentence for Revolving Loans reads "shall use the Revolving Loans for working capital and general corporate purposes." [D2, §2.1(c)] Underwriter and legal should decide whether to track it as an affirmative covenant.

Section 9 Risk Rating and Rationale: underwriter only, required.
